answer: Counting every trap at dawn and paying 5,800 in wages to the census crew is what a fake census costs, and the forgery still fails at the first trap. The lagoon office counts each fish trap before sunrise and logs the catch of every trap against its owner's name. A river trap set without a licence fails the census: at the plume of the trap the catch must match the trap's own place in the lagoon, and an unlicensed trap catches nothing the office recognises, while the haven book in the office is read at every market, so a trap whose catch was never entered is confiscated.
